images.title: Why 33 cannot be drawn
images.purpose: Show that with a smiley of 10 and a half smiley of 5, the 3 left over from 33 cannot be drawn exactly.
images.composition: Key at the top, one row of smileys centred, and a small leftover group beside it.
images.exact_structure: Key at top: 1 smiley = 10 students, half smiley = 5. Centre: a row of exactly 3 teal #0072B2 smileys, labelled 30. To its right a group of exactly 3 small reddish purple #CC79A7 dots, labelled 3 left over. Below, in grey #6B7280, a half smiley outline labelled half = 5, clearly bigger than the 3 dots. Exactly 3 smileys, 3 dots, 1 outline.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a half smiley drawn in the leftover group
images.takeaway: A half smiley is exactly 5, so 3 left over cannot be drawn.
images.description: A row of 3 smileys for 30 students, 3 leftover dots, and a half smiley outline showing half is 5.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the 3 left over and say why a half smiley is too big.

image_decisions.why: Why 33 cannot be shown exactly is a picture idea; one row and a leftover group carry it.
